description: The complete interface implemented by ob, the OpenBindings reference tool. One unbound contract describing everything ob does: creating, inspecting, editing, validating, comparing, and invoking OpenBindings interfaces, plus context storage and environment management. This document carries no bindings or sources; it is the single source of truth from which the per-surface realizations (CLI via usage, server via OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/MCP) are derived, so they cannot drift. An operation that realizes a published OpenBindings interface is keyed by that interface's operation name (e.g. openbindings.kv-store.set), so satisfaction needs no alias; ob's own operations are keyed under the ob namespace (e.g. ob.syncInterface). Aliases appear only where one operation satisfies more than one published interface, as listFormats does.
name: ob

openbindings.ob.assessCompatibility.description: Assess whether a candidate interface conforms to a target interface and produce a report: per-operation input/output slot status, overall conformance level, and coverage. A report, not a binary verdict.

openbindings.ob.codegen.description: Generate a typed invoker for an interface in a target language (TypeScript or Go). The output is an invoker over the cardinality-agnostic handle, not a cardinality-specific client.

openbindings.ob.compareInterfaces.description: Structurally compare two interfaces (or one interface against what its sources produce) and report the differences per operation and metadata field, including cross-source drift.

openbindings.ob.conform.description: Scaffold a target interface so it conforms to a reference interface: add the operations the reference requires and reconcile mismatches, returning the updated target and a report of each change. With dryRun, reports the changes without applying them.

openbindings.ob.deleteContext.description: Delete the stored context for a key. Deleting an absent key succeeds.

openbindings.ob.describe.description: Return identity and metadata about ob: name, version, description, homepage, repository, maintainer.

openbindings.ob.getContext.description: Get the stored context for a key. Returns the unified context payload (credentials, headers, cookies, environment, metadata in a single opaque map), or null when no context exists for the key.

openbindings.ob.getDelegateRequirements.description: Return the published interface a delegate must satisfy to provide a capability (invoke → binding-invoker, create → interface-synthesizer, inspect → source-inspector), so a prospective delegate can be checked against the exact contract (e.g. via assessCompatibility). The interfaces are immutable documents bundled with this ob release.

openbindings.ob.getEnvironmentStatus.description: Report a snapshot of the active OpenBindings environment (the .openbindings/ directory): whether it is local or global, its path, and counts of the delegates and contexts it holds.

openbindings.ob.getInterfaceStatus.description: Report an interface's status against its sources: per-source sync state (in-sync, managed, what a sync would change) and the managed-vs-hand-authored breakdown of its operations and bindings. Read-only — distinct from syncInterface (which re-derives and writes) and from compareInterfaces with fromSources (which reports raw differences).

openbindings.ob.inspectSource.description: Inspect a binding source artifact and report the bindable targets it contains, before any interface is created. Lets tooling show a user what an artifact offers.

openbindings.ob.invokeBinding.description: Invoke a resolved binding via a typed bidirectional I/O frame stream (the binding-invoker frame protocol). The caller streams BindingInvokerInputFrame messages (one `open` carrying the BindingInvocationInput, zero or more `input`, one `close`); the service streams BindingInvokerOutputFrame messages back (zero or more `output`/`input_closed`, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`). One shape covers unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional bindings; cardinality is observed by how the caller drives the frames. Missing runtime context fails with a terminal CONTEXT_REQUIRED error carrying ContextRequiredDetails, before any output and any side effect.

openbindings.ob.listContexts.description: List non-secret metadata summaries for all stored contexts; never returns secret values. Completes the context surface with listing and inspection: the generic kv-store substrate these contexts are stored under (satisfied by getContext/setContext/deleteContext) standardizes only opaque get/set/delete, so this management view is ob's own.

openbindings.ob.listDelegates.description: List the registered delegates with the capabilities and formats each provides. Capabilities (invoke/create/inspect) and formats are discovered from each delegate's OBI.

openbindings.ob.listFormats.description: List the binding formats this instance can handle. One operation satisfies the listFormats slot of every interface that has one, since the answer is the same regardless of which capability is asking.

openbindings.ob.mergeInterfaces.description: Selectively apply changes from one interface (or from the target's own sources) into another, and return the merged interface alongside a report of what was applied and skipped.

openbindings.ob.prepareBinding.description: Preflight a binding: report the context it would require before invocation, without invoking it or causing side effects. Returns ContextRequiredDetails the runtime can resolve proactively, or null when requirements cannot be determined statically. Advisory; invokeBinding's reactive CONTEXT_REQUIRED error is authoritative. When context is supplied, reports only the requirements still unsatisfied by it.

openbindings.ob.resolveInterface.description: Resolve an OpenBindings interface from a URL or host. Performs well-known discovery, follows redirects, and synthesizes an OBI from a raw binding spec (e.g. an OpenAPI document) when the target is not already an OBI. Returns the interface and metadata about how it was resolved.

openbindings.ob.setContext.description: Create or replace the context for a key. The supplied value fully replaces any existing context (full replacement, not partial update).

openbindings.ob.synthesizeInterface.description: Create an OpenBindings interface, optionally from binding source artifacts. Given one or more sources (e.g. an OpenAPI spec, a CLI usage spec), extracts operations, schemas, sources, and bindings into the new OBI; with no sources, produces an empty interface to author by hand.

openbindings.ob.validateInterface.description: Validate an OpenBindings interface document against the specification. Reports whether it is valid, the declared spec version, and any problems. With strict mode, rejects unknown fields and requires a supported version.

info.description: WebSocket API for the OpenBindings CLI (ob start): the invokeBinding operation of the binding-invoker interface as a typed I/O frame stream. Clients upgrade /bindings/invoke to a WebSocket; one connection carries exactly one invocation. The caller streams BindingInvokerInputFrame messages (exactly one `open` first, zero or more `input`, one `close`); the server streams BindingInvokerOutputFrame messages back (zero or more `output` / `input_closed`, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`). One shape covers unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional bindings.
info.title: ob start streaming API

invokeBinding.description: Open a WebSocket to /bindings/invoke (token on the upgrade request; see the bearer security scheme). Stream BindingInvokerInputFrame messages: exactly one `open` frame first (anything else is a terminal ERR_PROTOCOL), then zero or more `input` frames, then one `close`. The server streams BindingInvokerOutputFrame messages: `output` frames as the binding produces values, an `input_closed` frame if the binding closes the input side from its end (later `input` frames are ignored, never written; the invocation continues), and exactly one terminal frame — `complete` or `error`. Input frames with unknown properties are rejected with ERR_PROTOCOL. If the transport closes without a terminal frame, the consumer synthesizes ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED. Missing runtime context fails with a terminal CONTEXT_REQUIRED error whose details enumerate the requirements, before any output and any side effect.
